applied.problem: 2.23 V is one maker's vented float at 20 °C; parallel strings share inversely to resistance only at equal voltage; 'empties first' overstates it, as the share shifts while the busier string sags; overcharge contributes to grid corrosion; the tanks count charge in as charge out.
Specific gravity can only be read on vented (flooded) cells, not sealed ones; and the rule of thumb on parallel sharing holds only when the strings' voltages match, as the parallel card assumes.

2.23 V should be named as one maker's vented float at 20 °C (its source); 'String A ... empties first' overstates what equal-voltage parallel strings do; and the source says prolonged overcharge contributes to grid corrosion, not that it alone corrodes.
